qa.question: Is a "while your opponent has no Digimon with XX" condition also met when my opponent has no Digimon?
qa.answer: Yes, it's met.

qa.question: If there are 6 cards in my security stack, does this card’s effect grant +2000 DP?
qa.answer:
No, it can't.
This effect can't be used on Digimon in the breeding area.

qa.question: When this card is placed in one of my Digimon’s digivolution cards, does this card’s inherited effect activate?
qa.answer: Yes, it does.

qa.question: Does this card's inherited effect activate when one of my own effects trashes a card from my deck?
qa.answer: Yes, it does.

qa.question: One of my effects reveals cards from the top of my deck and trashes one or more of them. Does this cause this card’s inherited effect to activate?
qa.answer: No, cards revealed from the top of your deck aren't considered to be “trashed from your deck,” so this card’s inherited effect doesn’t activate.

qa.question: Due to an effect, this Digimon has another [BT10-011 Canoweissmon] and a [BT8-008 Gammamon] under it as its digivolution cards. If I play a red Tamer, how exactly does [BT8-008 Gammamon]'s "When you play a red Tamer, <Draw 1> (Draw 1 card from your deck)" effect work in this situation?
qa.answer: This card's effect and inherited effect mean that this Digimon gains [BT8-008 Gammamon]'s effects twice, so <Draw 1> is activated twice and you draw a total of 2 cards.

qa.question: Can this card’s effect add a２-color Option card to my hand if one of its colors is red?
qa.answer: Yes, it can.

qa.question: Can this card’s effect add a card with a "this Digimon is also treated as red" effect to my hand?
qa.answer: No. Effects don't activate for cards revealed from your deck.

qa.question: If I have 2 yellow Digimon in play, does this effect reduce this card’s play cost by 2?
qa.answer: No. Even if you have 2 yellow Digimon in play, this effect can only reduce the play cost by a maximum of 1.

qa.question: After this Digimon gets +3000 DP from the [When Attacking] effect, its <Armor Purge> activates. What happens to the +3000 DP?
qa.answer: The effect has already been activated, so the +3000 DP effect persists for the turn.

qa.question: I digivolve a [BT8-013 BetelGammamon] into a [BT8-084 Kimeramon] and place this card as one of [BT8-084 Kimeramon]'s digivolution cards with its [When Digivolving] effect. Can I now activate [BT8-013 BetelGammamon]'s [When Digivolving] <Blitz> effect through this card's inherited effect and attack?
qa.answer: No, you can't. If this card is added to digivolution cards by [BT8-084 Kimeramon]'s [When Digivolving] effect, you get [BT8-013 BetelGammamon]'s <Blitz> effect through this card, but the time to trigger <Blitz> has already passed, so <Blitz> doesn't activate.

qa.question: Does this card’s [Your Turn] effect also count this Digimon itself as a Digimon with [Tyrannomon] in its name, granting it <Security Attack +1>?
qa.answer: Yes, it does.

qa.question: I have this card in the battle area, and it's suspended. Can my opponent's BT8-018 [Marsmon] attack their unsuspended Digimon?
qa.answer:
No, it can't attack.
If a "can" or "may" effect activates at the same timing as a "can't" effect, the "can't" effect takes precedence.

qa.question: How does this card’s [When Digivolving] effect work, exactly?
qa.answer: Your opponent chooses 1 of their Digimon. Next, delete all Digimon in play, from both you and your opponent, except for this Digimon and the Digimon your opponent chose. Then you gain 1 memory for every Digimon that was deleted by this effect.

qa.question: Does this card’s [When Digivolving] effect delete Digimon in breeding areas, too?
qa.answer: No, Digimon in breeding areas cannot be affected by effects, so they aren't deleted.

qa.question: For this card’s [When Digivolving] effect, can my opponent choose a Digimon in their breeding area?
qa.answer: No, Digimon in breeding areas cannot be affected by effects, so they can't be chosen. Additionally, note that this effect doesn't delete Digimon in breeding areas, regardless of whether they could be chosen or not.

qa.question: How does this card’s [When Digivolving] effect work if my opponent has no Digimon in play?
qa.answer: All of your other Digimon besides this one are deleted, and you gain 1 memory for each Digimon deleted in this way.

qa.question: When this card's [When Digivolving] effect deletes Digimon in play, can you and your opponent activate <Decoy>, <Armor Purge>, and similar effects to prevent their deletion?
qa.answer: Yes, you can.

qa.question: How does this card’s inherited effect work, exactly?
qa.answer: At the end of your turn, this effect allows you to DNA digivolve a Digimon with this card in its digivolution cards, along with one of your other Digimon, into a Digimon in your hand that has [DNA Digivolution]. Note that this happens before it becomes your opponent’s turn.

qa.question: With this card's inherited effect, can I DNA digivolve into a Digimon card in my hand that doesn't have [DNA Digivolution]?
qa.answer: No. You can't ignore the digivolution requirements, so you can’t DNA digivolve into a Digimon card that doesn't have [DNA Digivolution].

qa.question: Does this card's inherited effect allow me to DNA digivolve into a card other than the Digimon specified by [DNA Digivolution] in the hand?
qa.answer: No. You can’t ignore the digivolution requirements, so you can’t DNA digivolve using Digimon that aren’t specified in [DNA Digivolution].

qa.question: Can this card's effect add a 2-color Option card to my hand if one of its colors is blue?
qa.answer: Yes, you can.

qa.question: Can this card’s effect add a card with a "this Digimon is also treated as blue" effect to my hand?
qa.answer: No. Effects don't activate for cards revealed from your deck.

qa.question: If BT8-022 [SnowAgumon]'s [On Play] effect is used to choose a Digimon without digivolution cards, can that effect's trashing be replaced by this card's [Opponent's Turn] effect?
qa.answer:
Yes, it can.
Once replaced, you choose and trash 2 digivolution cards of this card.

qa.question: My opponent doesn't have any Digimon with digivolution cards in play, meaning this card's [When Digivolving] effect can't trash the bottom digivolution card of 1 of my opponent's Digimon. Do I still activate the "1 of your opponent's Digimon with no digivolution cards gets -3000 DP for the turn" part of the effect?
qa.answer: Yes. Even if you can't trash any of your opponent’s digivolution cards, you still get to give -3000 DP to 1 of their Digimon with no digivolution cards.

qa.question: When this card's [Your turn] effect activates and I <Recovery +1 (Deck)>, when exactly does this happen?
qa.answer: The effect triggers "when this Digimon would digivolve," so it occurs after declaring the digivolution, but before paying the digivolution cost.

qa.question: Does this card’s effect activate when your opponent’s Digimon digivolves to level 5 or higher?
qa.answer: No, digivolving doesn't count as playing a card, so the effect doesn't activate.

qa.question: Does this card’s effect activate when your opponent moves a level 5 or higher Digimon from the breeding area to the battle area?
qa.answer: No, moving a Digimon from your breeding area doesn't count as playing it, so the effect doesn't activate.

qa.question: If my opponent has a Digimon with digivolution cards in their breeding area, can this Digimon attack?
qa.answer: Yes. Digimon in breeding areas aren’t counted by the effect, so this Digimon can attack.

qa.question: Does this card’s inherited effect activate when my opponent activates <Digi-Burst>?
qa.answer: Yes, it does.

qa.question: If both blue and green cards are in this card’s digivolution cards, do I activate both parts of this card’s [When Attacking] effect?
qa.answer: Yes, you do.

qa.question: If a single blue and green multicolor card is in this card’s digivolution cards, do I activate both parts of this card’s [When Attacking] effect?
qa.answer: Yes, you do.

qa.question: Can I use this card’s effect to add a two-color Option card to my hand if one of its colors is yellow?
qa.answer: Yes, it can.

qa.question: Can this card’s effect add a card with a "this Digimon is also treated as yellow" effect to my hand?
qa.answer: No. Effects don't activate for cards revealed from your deck.

qa.question: If the Digimon with this card in its digivolution cards is itself blue, does this card’s inherited effect activate?
qa.answer: Yes, it does.

qa.question: After I use this card’s [When Digivolving] effect to gain +2000 DP for each card with [Armor Form] in its traits in my trash, I use <Armor Purge> to trash this card. What happens to the DP boost?
qa.answer: The effect has already been activated, so the DP boost persists for the turn.

qa.question: If I have 2 Tamers in play, can this card's [When Digivolving] effect give up to 6 of my opponent's Digimon -5000 DP?
qa.answer: No. No matter how many Tamers you have in play, the effect gives -5000 DP to up to 3 of your opponent's Digimon.

qa.question: This card's effect trashes a red card in my hand. Does this make this Digimon a red/yellow 2-color Digimon, allowing me to <Draw 2>?
qa.answer: Yes, the Digimon is now treated as having two colors, so you <Draw 2>.

qa.question: This card's effect trashes a blue/green multicolor card in my hand. Does this make this Digimon a yellow/blue/green 3-color Digimon?
qa.answer: Yes, the Digimon is now treated as having three colors.

qa.question: If I have multiple Tamers in play, can this card's [On Play][When Digivolving] effect give <Security Attack -2> to a different one of my opponent’s Digimon for each Tamer I have in play?
qa.answer: Yes. The effect activates for each Tamer you have in play, and you can choose a different target for each activation.

qa.question: When I activate this card’s [On Play][When Digivolving] effect multiple times, is each activation treated as its own timing?
qa.answer: No, it’s treated as a single timing.

qa.question: I digivolve one of my suspended Digimon into this Digimon. Does this card's [Your Turn] effect let me unsuspend this Digimon itself?
qa.answer:
No, it doesn't.
This Digimon's [Your Turn] effect only triggers when your other Digimon digivolve.

qa.question: If I choose an opponent's Digimon for this card's [When Digivolving] effect, and that Digimon loses <Blocker> due to digivolving, <De-Digivolve>, or some other reason, can that Digimon now attack and block again?
qa.answer: No. Once a Digimon with <Blocker> is targeted by this card's [When Digivolving] effect, it becomes unable to attack or block until the end of your opponent’s next turn, even if it loses <Blocker>.

qa.question: With this card's [When Digivolving] effect, can I suspend this Digimon itself in order to suspend 1 of my opponent's Digimon?
qa.answer: Yes, you can.

qa.question: If BT8-053 [Lighdramon] and P-117 [Veemon] are revealed by this card's [On Play] effect, can I choose BT8-053 [Lighdramon] to add as the blue card but choose to not add P-117 [Veemon] to my hand?
qa.answer: Yes, you can.

qa.question: Can I activate this card's [Your Turn] effect before my opponent's Digimon unsuspends in the unsuspend phase due to <Reboot>?
qa.answer: Yes, you can. Digimon with <Reboot> unsuspend at the same time as the current player's turn. This effect activates "if this Digimon is unsuspended", so it activates immediately after.

qa.question: My opponent has this Digimon in play. During my turn, I use an Option card like [BT1-109 Smashed Potatoes] or [EX1-071 Win Rate: 60%!] which has an effect that activates “the next time one of your Digimon digivolves”. After that, all of my opponent’s Digimon become suspended. If I then digivolve one of my Digimon, are the effects from the Option cards I used earlier negated?
qa.answer: No. You already used the Option cards and activated their effects, so this card’s [Opponent’s Turn] effect can’t negate them.

qa.question: My opponent has this Digimon in play. If I have an Option card with <Delay> that I used from my hand earlier, can I activate its <Delay> effect?
qa.answer:
Yes, you can.
Activating <Delay> on Option cards that are already in your battle area doesn't count as using an Option card.

qa.question: What does a "players can't ignore digivolution requirements" effect do, exactly?
qa.answer:
This effect prevents players from ignoring digivolution requirements.
This effect affects both players.

qa.question: Is DNA digivolution or Burst Digivolve possible while a "players can't ignore digivolution requirements" effect is activated?
qa.answer: Yes, DNA digivolution and Burst Digivolve are possible.

qa.question: Is digivolution without paying the cost possible while a "players can't ignore digivolution requirements" effect is activated?
qa.answer:
Yes, such digivolving is still possible.
Digivolving without paying the cost isn't the same as ignoring the digivolution requirements.

qa.question: If a "players can't ignore digivolution requirements" effect is activated, is digivolution possible using effects such as those that ignore parts of the digivolution requirements such as levels?
qa.answer: No, players can’t ignore part of the digivolution requirements.

qa.question: Is digivolution using BT10-067 [Justimon: Critical Arm]'s [When Attacking] effect possible while a "players can't ignore digivolution requirements" effect is activated?
qa.answer: No, such digivolution isn't possible.

qa.question: Is digivolution from a Tamer using BT4-011 [Agunimon]'s 1st effect possible while a "players can't ignore digivolution requirements" effect is activated?
qa.answer:
Yes, such digivolution is possible.
Effects that add to card information for digivolution aren't the same as effects that ignore digivolution requirements.

qa.question: What does this card's (Rule) mean, exactly? (*This card's "The name of this card/Digimon is also treated as [Mamemon]" has been changed to "(Rule) Name: Also treated as [Mamemon].")
qa.answer: This is a special rule for this card that always treats it as if it also has the [Mamemon] name.

qa.question: What does this card's (Rule) mean, exactly? (*This card's "The name of this card/Digimon is also treated as [SkullKnightmon] and [DeadlyAxemon]" has been changed to "(Rule) Name: Also treated as [SkullKnightmon] and [DeadlyAxemon].")
qa.answer: This is a special rule for this card that always treats it as if it also has the [SkullKnightmon] and [DeadlyAxemon] names.

qa.question: If the Digimon with this card in its digivolution cards is itself red, does this card’s inherited effect activate?
qa.answer: Yes, it does.

qa.question: Can this card's effect add a total of up to 4 Digimon cards with [Mamemon] in their names from both my hand and/or trash to the top of my deck?
qa.answer: Yes, you can add up to 4 cards in any combination from your hand and/or trash.

qa.question: Can this card's [Your Turn] effect digivolve it into any Digimon card regardless of digivolution requirements, so long as it has [X Antibody] in its traits?
qa.answer: No. Digivolution requirements cannot be ignored unless an effect explicitly instructs you to ignore them.

qa.question: How does this card’s [When Digivolving] effect work if my opponent has no Digimon in play?
qa.answer:
You can reveal 3 cards, then trash all of them.
Note that the effect reads, “you may,” so you can choose whether or not to activate the effect when digivolving, regardless of whether or not your opponent has any Digimon in play. If you choose not to activate it, you don't reveal or trash any cards.

qa.question: What does “memory cost of 10 or less” refer to?
qa.answer: Play cost.

changes.before: [Your Turn][Once Per Turn] When one of your effects places a digivolution card under this Digimon, this Digimon gets +2000 DP and can't be deleted by your opponent's effects until the end of your opponent's next turn.
changes.after: [Your Turn][Once Per Turn] When one of your effects places a digivolution card under one of your Digimon, this Digimon gets +2000 DP and can't be deleted by your opponent's effects until the end of your opponent's next turn.

errata.notes: Read as the errata when playing.

changes.before: [All Turns][Once Per Turn] When an opponent's Digimon is deleted, unsuspend this Digimon.
changes.after: [All Turns][Once Per Turn] When an opponent's Digimon is deleted, you may unsuspend this Digimon.

errata.notes: Read as the errata when playing.

qa.question: If this card has both red and black digivolution cards, can this card's [When Digivolving] effect delete both Digimon and Tamers?
qa.answer: Yes, it can.

qa.question: If this card has both red and black digivolution cards, can this card's [When Digivolving] effect delete both 6 play cost worth of my opponent’s Digimon, and 6 play cost worth of my opponent’s Tamers?
qa.answer: No. The total play costs of the chosen Digimon and Tamers must add up to 6 or less.

qa.question: If a single red and black multicolor card is in this card’s digivolution cards, can I activate both parts of this card’s [When Digivolving] effect?
qa.answer: Yes, you can.

qa.question: What does "players can't reduce play costs" mean, exactly?
qa.answer: This effect prevents costs from being reduced when play costs are to be paid. This effect affects both players.

qa.question: If a "players can't reduce play costs" effect has activated, can a card be played using a "play without paying the cost" effect?
qa.answer:
Yes, it can be played.
"Play this card without paying the cost" effects aren't effects that reduce the play cost.

qa.question: If a "players can't reduce play costs" effect has activated, can a play cost be reduced using an effect on a Digimon in the breeding area?
qa.answer:
No, play costs can't be reduced.
A "players can't reduce play costs" effect isn't an effect that affects cards that activate play-cost-reducing effects, it's an effect that affects players. Therefore, the target players can't reduce play costs.

qa.question: If a "players can't reduce play costs" effect has activated, is DigiXrosing possible?
qa.answer:
Yes, DigiXrosing is possible.
However, it isn't possible to reduce play costs through DigiXrosing. Therefore, a player can't declare to play a card in a state where its play cost can't be paid.

qa.question: My opponent has [BT8-071 Psychemon] in play. Can this Digimon’s [Your Turn] effect still reduce the play cost of cards with [D-Reaper] in their traits when I would play them?
qa.answer: No. [BT8-071 Psychemon]’s effect doesn’t target Digimon themselves, so you can’t activate this card's effect to reduce the play cost of cards.

qa.question: The memory is at 0, and my opponent has 2 Digimon including BT8-071 [Psychemon] in the battle area. Can I declare to play this card, then suspend my opponent's 2 Digimon including BT8-071 [Psychemon]?
qa.answer:
No, you can't.
You can't pay the cost because you can't use BT8-071 [Psychemon]'s effect to reduce it, therefore you can't declare to play this card in the first place.

qa.question: The memory is at 1 or more, and my opponent has 2 Digimon including BT8-071 [Psychemon] in the battle area. Can I declare to play this card, then suspend my opponent's 2 Digimon including BT8-071 [Psychemon]?
qa.answer:
Yes, you can.
You can't use BT8-071 [Psychemon]'s effect to reduce the play cost, but the original play cost can be paid, therefore you can declare to play this card.
After declaring to play it, you can use the 1st effect to suspend 2 Digimon, but you can't reduce the play cost, therefore you must pay the original play cost of 11 in order to play this card.

qa.question: If I reveal a non-purple Digimon card with this card’s [On Play] effect, can I trash it?
qa.answer: No. This card’s effect can only trash purple Digimon cards.

qa.question: Is this card’s effect triggered by the activation of an effect that reads, “Reveal the top X cards of your deck... Trash the remaining cards.”?
qa.answer: No, cards revealed from the top of your deck aren't considered to be “trashed from your deck,” so this card’s effect doesn’t trigger.

qa.question: Is this card’s inherited effect triggered by the activation of an effect that reads, “Reveal the top X cards of your deck... Trash the remaining cards.”?
qa.answer: No, cards revealed from the top of your deck aren't considered to be “trashed from your deck,” so this card’s effect doesn’t trigger.

qa.question: If both purple and yellow cards are in this card’s digivolution cards, can I activate both parts of this card’s [When Digivolving] effect?
qa.answer: Yes, you can.

qa.question: If a single purple and yellow multicolor card is in this card’s digivolution cards, can I activate both parts of this card’s [When Digivolving] effect?
qa.answer: Yes, you can.

qa.question: I activated this card's [On Play] effect, and when my opponent's Digimon would leave the battle area for the 1st process, an immediate-type effect such as a "when [...] would leave" effect caused this card to be removed from the battle area. Can I then process the rest of this effect?
qa.answer:
Yes, you can.
If an effect activates, it is to be fully resolved even if the card that activated the effect is removed from that area during the processing.

qa.question: How does this card’s [Your Turn] effect work, exactly?
qa.answer:
The effect allows this card to be treated as both white (its original color), and as the colors of its digivolution cards.
For example, if a red card and green card are in this card’s digivolution cards, this card is treated as a 3-color white/red/green card.

qa.question: I digivolve a [BT8-013 BetelGammamon] into a [BT8-084 Kimeramon] and place this card as one of [BT8-084 Kimeramon]'s digivolution cards with its [When Digivolving] effect. Can I now activate [BT8-013 BetelGammamon]'s [When Digivolving] <Blitz> effect through this card's inherited effect and attack?
qa.answer: No, you can't. If this card is added to digivolution cards by [BT8-084 Kimeramon]'s [When Digivolving] effect, you get [BT8-013 BetelGammamon]'s <Blitz> effect through this card, but the time to trigger <Blitz> has already passed, so <Blitz> doesn't activate.

qa.question: This card has an effect that reads, “When one of your Digimon with 2 or more colors attacks”―does this include the colors of the attacking Digimon’s digivolution cards?
qa.answer: No. The effect can only be activated if the Digimon itself has 2 or more colors.

qa.question: Is this card’s [Opponent’s Turn] effect triggered when I block an opponent’s attack with one of my blue Digimon?
qa.answer: No. The effect only triggers when your opponent chooses one of your blue Digimon as a target of attack.

qa.question: Can I activate both parts of this card’s [Start of Your Main Phase] effect if I have both a blue Digimon and green Digimon in play?
qa.answer: Yes, you can.

qa.question: If I have a single blue and green multicolor Digimon in play, can I activate both parts of this card’s [Start of Your Main Phase] effect?
qa.answer: Yes, you can.

qa.question: This card's effect reveals 3 cards. If a [BT8-088 Davis Motomiya & Ken Ichijoji] is among the cards revealed, can I add that card to my hand?
qa.answer: Yes, it's a Tamer card with [Davis Motomiya] in its name, so you can add it to your hand.

qa.question: This card has an effect that reads, “When one of your Digimon with 2 or more colors attacks”―does this include the colors of the attacking Digimon’s digivolution cards?
qa.answer: No. The effect can only be activated if the Digimon itself has 2 or more colors.

qa.question: Does this card’s [Opponent’s Turn] effect activate when an effect from a card like [BT1-089 Mimi Tachikawa] moves a level 3 Digimon from your opponent's breeding area to their battle area outside of their breeding phase?
qa.answer: Yes, it does.

qa.question: During the breeding phase, I move a Digimon from the breeding area to the battle area and due to this card's [Opponent's Turn] effect of my opponent, and the memory gauge moves to 1 or more on my opponent's side. In this case, do I have a main phase?
qa.answer: No, the main phase doesn't take place and the turn ends.

qa.question: I used this card's [Main] effect to give <Security A. +1> to one of my Digimon with <Armor Purge>, then that Digimon attacked and checked 1 security card. At such times, if that Digimon loses a battle with a Security Digimon and would be deleted, but <Armor Purge> causes a stacked card to be trashed and prevents the deletion, is the additional security check performed?
qa.answer: Yes, you perform the additional security check.

qa.question: Does this card’s “If you have a Digimon in play with...2 or more colors in one of its digivolution cards” count a Digimon that has both a red card and a blue card in its digivolution cards?
qa.answer:
No, it doesn't.
The effect is looking for a Digimon with a digivolution card that has 2 or more colors.

qa.question: Does this card’s “If you have a Digimon in play with...2 or more colors in one of its digivolution cards” count a Digimon with a card like [BT3-040 Shakkoumon]’s “This Digimon is also treated as blue” in its digivolution cards?
qa.answer:
No, it doesn't.
Effects that grant additional colors don't do anything as digivolution cards, so the card is only treated as a single color.

changes.before: [Main] Delete all of your opponent's Digimon with 6000 DP or less. Your opponent can't play Digimon by effects until the end of their next turn.
changes.after: [Main] Your opponent can't play Digimon by effects until the end of their turn. Delete all of your opponent's Digimon with 6000 DP or less.

errata.notes: Read as the errata when playing.

qa.question: If my opponent has 7 or more Digimon in play, does this card’s effect get reduced to negative 1, effectively gaining me a memory for using it?
qa.answer:
No. It just reduces the cost of the card to 0.
Note that in general, costs can’t be reduced to less than 0.

qa.question: I use this card, then attack my opponent. During the security check, I flip over a Digimon card with the effect, “[Security] At the end of the battle, play this card without paying its memory cost.” What happens to this Security Digimon?
qa.answer: After the battle between the attacking Digimon and Security Digimon, the effect prevents the Digimon from being played, so it's placed in the trash.

qa.question: My opponent used this card on my [BT7-063 DarkKnightmon]. [DarkKnightmon]'s [All Turns] effect is a "when this Digimon would be deleted" effect that interrupts deletion when it activates, but can I use this card's "your opponent can't play Digimon by effects until the end of their turn" effect to prevent [SkullKnightmon] and [DeadlyAxemon] from being played from [DarkKnightmon]'s digivolution cards?
qa.answer:
Yes, they can't be played.
This card's [Main] effect was changed to "Your opponent can't play Digimon by effects until the end of their turn. Delete all of your opponent's Digimon with 6000 DP or less." Therefore, first the effect that prevents playing Digimon is applied, then Digimon with 6000 DP or less are deleted.
Please see the notices regarding changes to the rules/rulings on the official website.

qa.question: If this card's effect is activated on the opponent's turn, how long does the effect last?
qa.answer: When the effect of this card is activated on the opponent's turn, it lasts until the end of that turn.

qa.question: An Option card's use cost is 1 or less when used from the hand due to an effect such as BT2-099 [Glorious Burst] or BT8-097 [Crimson Blaze]'s 1st effect. When such a card is used, does this card's "when you use an Option card with a use cost of 2 or more" effect trigger?
qa.answer:
No, it doesn't trigger.
If a card's cost itself is reduced when it's used from the hand, it's considered to be using an Option card with a use cost after the reduction is applied. Therefore, the "when you use an Option card with a use cost of 2 or more" effect doesn't trigger.

qa.question: Can I use this card's [All Turns] effect to play a [Petrification] Token during the turn I activated BT8-097 [Crimson Blaze]'s [Main] effect?
qa.answer:
Yes, you can.
This card's [All Turns] effect plays one of your cards.
Cards can be played by your effects even after a "your opponent can't play Digimon by effects" effect has activated.

qa.question: What does a "your opponent can't play XX by effects" effect do, exactly?
qa.answer:
Such effects prevent your opponent from playing XX by effects.
With this card's effect, your opponent can no longer play Digimon by effects such as BT10-018 [Gaossmon]'s [On Deletion] effect or BT16-048 [TyrantKabuterimon]'s [When Digivolving] effect.
This effect affects the opponent player.

qa.question: I activate a "your opponent can't play XX by effects" effect, and in the same turn, my opponent activates an effect that reveals cards and plays a specified card from their deck. Is the card revealed from the deck but not played?
qa.answer: Yes. Your opponent reveals cards, but then doesn't play the specified card.

qa.question: Can an opponent's Digimon be played if I activate a "your opponent can't play Digimon by effects" effect, and in the same turn, I activate an effect such as EX5-060 [Dragomon]'s [On Play] [When Digivolving] effect that plays an opponent's Digimon card?
qa.answer:
Yes, it can be played.
"Your opponent can't play Digimon by effects" is an effect that prevents your opponent from playing Digimon by effects. Your effects can still play an opponent's Digimon.

qa.question: Can my Digimon be played if I activate a "your opponent can't play Digimon by effects" effect, and in the same turn, my opponent activates an effect such as EX5-060 [Dragomon]'s [On Play] [When Digivolving] effect that plays an opponent's Digimon card?
qa.answer:
No, it can't be played.
"Your opponent can't play Digimon by effects" is an effect that prevents your opponent from playing Digimon by effects. Your Digimon can't be played by an opponent's effect.

qa.question: A card's cost is 0 when used from the hand due to an effect such as BT2-099 [Glorious Burst] or BT8-097 [Crimson Blaze]'s 1st effect. When such a card is used, does this card's "when you use an Option card with a use cost of 1 or more" effect trigger?
qa.answer:
No, it doesn't trigger.
If a card's cost itself is reduced when it's used from the hand, it's considered to be using an Option card with a use cost after the reduction is applied. Therefore, the "when you use an Option card with a use cost of 1 or more" effect doesn't trigger.

qa.question: An Option card's use cost is 5 or less when used from the hand due to an effect such as BT2-099 [Glorious Burst] or BT8-097 [Crimson Blaze]'s 1st effect. Can I use this card's [On Play] [When Digivolving] effect to place that card as a security card?
qa.answer:
Yes, you can.
If a card's use cost itself is reduced when it's used from the hand and the use cost is 5 or less, this card's [On Play] [When Digivolving] effect can place that card as a security card.

qa.question: Can I use this card's [When Digivolving] effect to play a [Petrification] Token during the turn I activated BT8-097 [Crimson Blaze]'s [Main] effect?
qa.answer:
Yes, it can be played.
This card's [When Digivolving] effect plays one of your cards.
Cards can be played by your effects even after a "your opponent can't play Digimon by effects" effect has activated.

qa.question: Can I use this card's [When Digivolving] [End of Attack] effect to play a [Petrification] Token during the turn I activated BT8-097 [Crimson Blaze]'s [Main] effect?
qa.answer:
Yes, it can be played.
This card's [When Digivolving] [End of Attack] effect plays one of your cards.
Cards can be played by your effects even after a "your opponent can't play Digimon by effects" effect has activated.

qa.question: If I activate this card's [Main] effect, can my opponent use an effect to play a Digimon into their breeding area?
qa.answer: No, you can't.

qa.question: I use this card, but my opponent has no Digimon without digivolution cards in play, so I can't specify any Digimon that can't attack or block. If my opponent later plays a Digimon without digivolution cards to their battle area, can I make that Digimon unable to attack or block?
qa.answer:
No, you can't.
You can only specify Digimon that can't attack or block at the time this card’s effect is activated.

qa.question: If this card's effect is activated on the opponent's turn, how long does the effect last?
qa.answer: When the effect of this card is activated on the opponent's turn, it lasts until the end of that turn.

qa.question: Does this card’s “If you have a Digimon in play with...2 or more colors in one of its digivolution cards” count a Digimon that has both a red card and a blue card in its digivolution cards?
qa.answer:
No, it doesn't.
The effect is looking for a Digimon with a digivolution card that has 2 or more colors.

qa.question: Does this card’s “If you have a Digimon in play with...2 or more colors in one of its digivolution cards” count a Digimon with a card like [BT3-040 Shakkoumon]’s “This Digimon is also treated as blue” in its digivolution cards?
qa.answer:
No, it doesn't.
Effects that grant additional colors don't do anything as digivolution cards, so the card is only treated as a single color.

qa.question: If I have 1 card with [Armor Form] in its traits in my trash, can I use this card's effect to give an opponent's Digimon -4000 DP, and then give it an additional -1000 DP with the second part of the effect?
qa.answer: Yes, that's correct.

qa.question: Can I use this card's effect to prevent 1 of my opponent's suspended Digimon or Tamers from unsuspending until the end of their turn?
qa.answer: No. You can choose 1 of your opponent’s suspended Digimon or Tamers with this card's effect, but if you didn't use this effect to suspend that card, the “can't unsuspend until the end of their next turn” part of the effect doesn't apply.

qa.question: What does “Choose any number of your opponent's Digimon whose play costs add up to 15 or less” mean, exactly?
qa.answer: You can choose any number of your opponent's Digimon, as long as the play costs of the chosen Digimon add up to 15 or less. For example, you could choose 1 Digimon with a play cost of 3 and 1 Digimon with a play cost of 12, or 1 Digimon with a play cost of 2 and 2 Digimon with play costs of 6.

qa.question: Can I choose fewer cards than possible, even if the play costs of the chosen cards add up to less than 15?
qa.answer: Yes. As long as the total play costs of the chosen cards is less than 15, you can choose as many or as few cards as you like. However, note that you must choose a minimum of 1 Digimon with a play cost of 15 or less.

qa.question: My opponent uses effects to reduce play costs or play Digimon for free. Are Digimon played with these effects counted as having reduced play costs or play costs of 0 by this effect?
qa.answer: No. Regardless of how a Digimon was played, only the play cost printed on the card is counted for this card’s effect.

qa.question: Can I choose fewer cards than possible, even if the play costs of the chosen cards add up to less than 15?
qa.answer: Yes. As long as the total play costs of the chosen cards is less than 15, you can choose as many or as few cards as you like.

qa.question: This card's effect reads, "Digimon with a memory cost of 6 or less," but which cost is this referring to?
qa.answer: The Digimon's play cost.

qa.question: If my opponent has no Digimon in play or no Digimon with a level less than or equal to one of my Digimon, can I still use this card’s effect to delete 1 of my Digimon?
qa.answer: Yes, you can.

changes.before: [Main] 1 of your opponent's Digimon gets -6000 DP for the turn. Then, play 1 purple or yellow Digimon card with 6000 DP or less from your trash without paying its memory cost.
changes.after: [Main] 1 of your opponent's Digimon gets -6000 DP for the turn. Then, you may play 1 purple or yellow Digimon card with 6000 DP or less from your trash without paying its memory cost.

errata.notes: Read as the errata when playing.

changes.before: [Security] Play 1 level 3 Digimon card with [Free] in its traits from your hand or trash without paying its memory cost.
changes.after: [Security] You may play 1 level 3 Digimon card with [Free] in its traits from your hand or trash without paying its memory cost.

errata.notes: Read as the errata when playing.

qa.question: I use this card to trash the top card of 1 of my Digimon with [Armor Form] in its traits. Can I then digivolve one of my other Digimon into a Digimon card in my hand with [Armor Form] in its traits?
qa.answer: Yes, you can. If you do, only the Digimon you chose to digivolve will unsuspend.

qa.question: I use this card to trash the top card of 1 of my Digimon with [Armor Form] in its traits. Can I then choose NOT to digivolve one of my other Digimon into a Digimon card in my hand with [Armor Form] in its traits?
qa.answer: Yes, you can. If you choose this option, however, no Digimon will be unsuspended with this effect.

qa.question: When using this card’s effect to digivolve into a Digimon in my hand with [Armor Form] in its traits, can I ignore its digivolution requirements?
qa.answer: No. Digivolution requirements cannot be ignored unless an effect explicitly instructs you to ignore them.

qa.question: If this card's [When Digivolving] effect trashes 8 cards from the top of my deck, can I play 2 level 5 or lower purple Digimon cards from my trash without paying their memory costs?
qa.answer: No. Even if you trash more than 4 cards with the effect, you can only play 1 level 5 or lower purple Digimon card.

qa.question: If I have 20 cards in my trash, does this card's [When Attacking] effect trash the top 6 cards of my opponent’s deck and give this Digimon +6000 DP?
qa.answer: Yes. The effect reads, “For every 10 cards in your trash,” so if you have 20 cards in your trash, you would trash the top 6 cards of your opponent’s deck and get +6000 DP.

comprehensive-0223.title: <Blocker>
comprehensive-0223.text:
16-5. <Blocker>
16-5-1. <Blocker> is a keyword effect that applies a rule that allows a Digimon with that effect to block. (For details, refer to 12 "Blocking")
16-5-2. <Blocker> is a persistent effect. (For details, refer to 15-8-2 "Persistent Effects")
16-5-3. Even if 1 Digimon has multiple instances of <Blocker>, the number of blocks that can be performed during the block timing is only 1.

comprehensive-0224.title: <Recovery>
comprehensive-0224.text:
16-6. <Recovery>
16-6-1. <Recovery> is a keyword effect where the specified number of cards from the specified area are placed face down on top of the security stack. This is shown on cards using text such as <Recovery +1>.
16-6-2. <Recovery> effects execute processing.

comprehensive-0225.title: <Piercing>
comprehensive-0225.text:
16-7. <Piercing>
16-7-1. <Piercing> is a keyword effect that reads "When this Digimon deletes your opponent's Digimon in battle while attacking, it checks security before the attack ends." (For details, refer to 13 "Security Checks")
16-7-2. <Piercing> is a trigger-type effect that triggers and activates when a Digimon with this effect battles an opponent's Digimon and the opponent's Digimon is deleted in battle. (For details, refer to 15-8-3 "Trigger- Type Effects")
16-7-3. The security check from using <Piercing> is mandatory.
16-7-4. <Piercing> is pending processing that is processed immediately before the transition to the end of attack timing. Therefore, it will trigger simultaneously with effects triggered by the battle, but it is processed before the end of the attack. (Example: If a Digimon with <Piercing> attacks and deletes a Digimon with an [On Deletion] effect in the battle, first the [On Deletion] effect is resolved, then <Piercing> is processed.)
16-7-5. Only 1 security check can be performed during a single attack, even if <Piercing> activates multiple times. However, if the number of cards that can be checked by the attacking Digimon is modified, that number of cards will be checked in a single security check.
16-7-6. If there are no Digimon to perform a security check at the point when <Piercing> is processed, a security check won't be possible.

comprehensive-0226.title: <Draw>
comprehensive-0226.text:
16-8. <Draw>
16-8-1. <Draw> is a keyword effect where a player draws the cards from their deck according to the number specified in the effect. This is shown on cards using text such as <Draw 1>.
16-8-2. <Draw> effects execute processing.
16-8-3. A draw from <Draw> is mandatory.

comprehensive-0227.title: <Jamming>
comprehensive-0227.text:
16-9. <Jamming>
16-9-1. <Jamming> is a keyword effect where a Digimon with this effect isn't deleted as a result of a battle with an opponent's Security Digimon.
16-9-2. <Jamming> is a persistent effect. (For details, refer to 15-8-2 "Persistent Effects")

comprehensive-0228.title: <Digisorption>
comprehensive-0228.text:
16-10. <Digisorption>
16-10-1. <Digisorption> is a keyword effect. When a digivolution into a Digimon card with this effect in the hand would occur, by suspending 1 of your Digimon, the digivolution cost is reduced according to the value specified in the effect. This is shown on cards using text such as <Digisorption -3>.
16-10-2. <Digisorption> is an immediate-type effect that triggers when a digivolution into a card with this effect in the hand would occur. (For details, refer to 15-8-5 "Immediate-Type Effects")
16-10-3. "By suspending 1 of your Digimon" in <Digisorption> is an optional processing condition. If the content of that condition is executed, the processing for "the digivolution cost is reduced" will be mandatory.
16-10-4. If 1 Digimon card has multiple instances of <Digisorption>, they overlap when they trigger.37 Multiple instances of <Digisorption> can be activated for a single digivolution.
16-10-5. <Digisorption> can be used to suspend a Digimon that will become a digivolution card.

comprehensive-0229.title: <Reboot>
comprehensive-0229.text:
16-11. <Reboot>
16-11-1. <Reboot> is a keyword effect where a Digimon with this effect is unsuspended during the opponent's unsuspend phase.
16-11-2. <Reboot> is a persistent effect. (For details, refer to 15-8-2 "Persistent Effects")
16-11-3. Even if 1 Digimon has multiple instances of <Reboot>, it is only unsuspended once during the opponent's unsuspend phase.
16-11-4. The unsuspending from <Reboot> is mandatory.
16-11-5. The unsuspending from <Reboot> is performed at the same time as the unsuspending of the turn player's Digimon. The unsuspends aren't performed in any particular order.

comprehensive-0230.title: <De-Digivolve>
comprehensive-0230.text:
16-12. <De-Digivolve>
16-12-1. <De-Digivolve> is a keyword effect where the player declares a number from 1 up to the number specified in the effect, then the declared number of cards are trashed from the chosen stack(s) of cards starting with the top card. This is shown on cards using text such as <De- Digivolve 1>.
16-12-2. <De-Digivolve> effects execute processing.
16-12-3. The trashing from <De-Digivolve> is mandatory. Once activated, a player can't choose to trash 0 cards.
16-12-4. <De-Digivolve> can't trash cards from level 3 cards or lower.
16-12-5. If multiple cards are trashed using 1 instance of <De- Digivolve>, all of the cards are considered to be trashed at the same time, but the procedure for trashing them is 1 card from the stack at a time.
16-12-6. When using <De-Digivolve> to trash multiple cards, even if the category of the top card changes while the trashing is still being performed, the trashing will continue until the declared number is trashed.
16-12-7. When separate instances of <De-Digivolve> are executed multiple times in a single effect, the processing is performed separately for each instance.
16-12-8. When separate instances of <De-Digivolve> are executed multiple times in a single effect, the state of the chosen card is confirmed after each single process for <De-Digivolve> ends. If an effect will be activated as a result of the confirmed state, it is then activated. (Example: When 3 instances of <De-Digivolve 1> are executed in a single effect, if the chosen card becomes an "unaffected by effects" card as a result of the 1st instance of <De-Digivolve 1>, that card is unaffected by the following instances of <De-Digivolve 1>.

comprehensive-0231.title: <Retaliation>
comprehensive-0231.text:
16-13. <Retaliation>
16-13-1. <Retaliation> is a keyword effect where a battled opponent's Digimon is deleted when a Digimon with this effect is deleted in battle.
16-13-2. <Retaliation> is a trigger-type effect that triggers when just the Digimon with this effect is deleted in battle. (For details, refer to 15-8-3 "Trigger-Type Effects")
16-13-3. The processing from <Retaliation> is mandatory.

comprehensive-0233.title: <Rush>
comprehensive-0233.text:
16-15. <Rush>
16-15-1. <Rush> is a keyword effect where the Digimon with this effect can also attack in the same turn it was played.
16-15-2. <Rush> is a persistent effect. (For details, refer to 15-8-2 "Persistent Effects")

comprehensive-0234.title: <Blitz>
comprehensive-0234.text:
16-16. <Blitz>
16-16-1. <Blitz> is a keyword effect where a Digimon with this effect can attack if your opponent has 1 or more memory.
16-16-2. <Blitz> effects execute processing.
16-16-3. <Blitz> has a processing condition that requires the memory to be at 1 or more on your opponent's side. "This Digimon may attack" is optional processing.
16-16-4. After using <Blitz> to make an attack declaration, the attack will proceed even if the memory moves to 0 or more.38
16-16-5. An attack can't be made using <Blitz> if the memory is at 0 or more upon activating <Blitz>.

comprehensive-0235.title: <Delay>
comprehensive-0235.text:
16-17. <Delay>
16-17-1. <Delay> is a keyword effect. While a card with this effect is in the battle area, by trashing that card, the effect specified in <Delay> will activate.
16-17-2. The processing from <Delay> is optional. (For details, refer to 15-7 "Optional Processing Conditions")
16-17-3. <Delay> can't be activated the same turn the card with the effect is placed in the battle area.

comprehensive-0236.title: <Decoy>
comprehensive-0236.text:
16-18. <Decoy>
16-18-1. <Decoy> is a keyword effect. When another of your specified Digimon would be deleted by an opponent's effect, by deleting the Digimon with this effect, <Decoy> prevents the Digimon specified by this effect from being deleted. This is shown on cards using text such as <Decoy (Black)>.
16-18-2. <Decoy> is an immediate-type effect that triggers when another of your Digimon specified by this effect would be deleted by an opponent's effect (For details, refer to 15-8-5 "Immediate-Type Effects")
16-18-3. "By deleting this Digimon" in <Decoy> is an optional processing condition. If the content of that condition is executed, the processing for "<Decoy> prevents the Digimon specified by this effect from being deleted" will be mandatory.

comprehensive-0237.title: <Armor Purge>
comprehensive-0237.text:
16-19. <Armor Purge>
16-19-1. <Armor Purge> is a keyword effect. When a Digimon with <Armor Purge> would be deleted, by trashing the top card of the Digimon with this effect, this effect prevents the deletion.
16-19-2. <Armor Purge> is an immediate-type effect that triggers when the Digimon with this effect would be deleted. (For details, refer to 15-8-5 "Immediate-Type Effects")
16-19-3. "By trashing the top card of the Digimon" in <Armor Purge> is an optional processing condition. If the content of that condition is executed, the processing for "prevents the deletion" will be mandatory.
